# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–9 (Complete and Final – Updated 86)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; **spring of third year (present narrative, now including crisis at Park Lane)** (narrative extends into future years); present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, hill farms of Coldcombe, Humdrum Hall, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Prince Regent locations, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, hill farms of Fenmere, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Hants, Life Guards, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Dunholt village, Bloomsbury, Russell Square, Harrowgate, Great Gaunt Street, village of Yarlton, hill farms of Mirecombe, parsonage, forge, Brompton, barracks neighbourhood, City church, Gloster Coffee House, Portsmouth, Queen's Crawley

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher; mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist
- **Secret Marriage**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church by special license; occurred as quiet, unobserved ceremony
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: Now living with Rawdon in snug little Brompton lodgings; trying new piano; wearing new gloves, shawls, rings, watch purchased by Rawdon; husband nervously awaits Miss Crawley's recovery
- **Role at Park Lane**: Originally companion/nurse to Miss Crawley; indispensable; controlled household access; maintained composed appearance; read Morning Post to Miss Crawley in bed mornings
- **Knowledge of Marriage Revelation**: Marriage secret revealed to Miss Crawley through letter found on Rebecca's pincushion (discovered by Miss Briggs early morning, contents reposing there probably all night); letter reinstated Miss Briggs as first confidante of Miss Crawley

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca in City church by special license
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: Living with Rebecca in Brompton lodgings furnished luxuriously (piano, flowers, luxury items); awaiting outcome of Miss Crawley's reaction to revealed marriage; nervous about potential disinheritance; asks Rebecca "suppose the old lady doesn't come to, eh, Becky?"
- **Descriptors**: Rebecca described him as man with "head enough for both of us" and assured his ultimate benefit from her plans

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces
- **Response to Marriage Revelation**: Gave final scream and fell back in faint upon learning Rebecca married to Rawdon; suffered one fit of hysterics succeeding another; doctor and apothecary summoned; forced to be taken back to room she had just quitted; confined to bed under care of Mrs. Bute Crawley as nurse
- **Ignorance Timeline**: Remained completely unaware of marriage throughout spring of third year until revelation by letter; believed only in "previous attachment"

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [NEW MAJOR PRESENCE]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; arrived at Park Lane by Portsmouth mail during morning of marriage revelation crisis
- **Actions and Claims**: Declared Rebecca "artful little hussy" of whom she always had suspicions; considered Rawdon profligate, lost, abandoned being; never could account for Miss Crawley's infatuation with him; asserted his awful conduct will open Miss Crawley's eyes to his real character; positioned herself as nurse to Miss Crawley; stated "Her relations ought to be round about her"; left Gloster Coffee House (where Portsmouth mail had set her down) and took vacant room at Park Lane establishment to attend Miss Crawley; took comfortable hot toast and tea upon arrival

**Miss Briggs** [CHARACTER]
- Witnessed Sir Pitt's proposal through keyhole with Mrs. Firkin; now deeply attached to Rebecca's cause; found letter on Rebecca's pincushion containing marriage revelation early morning of crisis; read "affecting and interesting document" which reinstated her as first confidante of Miss Crawley; reported intelligence of clandestine marriage to Mrs. Bute upon her arrival; participated in preparation of Miss Crawley for news; shuddered and left room when Sir Pitt heard news and broke into fury

**Sir Pitt Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; now widower; made marriage proposal to Rebecca; knows Rebecca is married but not to whom; maintained friendly relations with her
- **Response to Marriage Revelation**: Upon learning Rebecca married to his son Rawdon, broke out into fury of language; sent poor Briggs shuddering from room; became frenzied old man, wild with hatred and insane with baffled desire
- **Subsequent Action**: One day after hearing news at Queen's Crawley, burst like madman into room Rebecca had used; dashed open her boxes with foot; flung about her papers, clothes, and other relics; Miss Horrocks (butler's daughter) took some; children dressed themselves and acted plays in others (occurred only few days after Lady Crawley's burial)

**Betty Martin** [NEW CHARACTER]
- Young woman from Hampshire, employed at Park Lane establishment under Mrs. Firkin's orders; business included knocking at Miss Sharp's door with jug of hot water; brother in Captain Crawley's troop; aware of "certain arrangements" which have great deal to do with this history; purchased yellow shawl, pair of green boots, light blue hat with red feather with three guineas from Rebecca (noted as bribery for "services rendered" given Rebecca's not liberal nature with money)

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Rebecca's former schoolfriend; small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul; confirmed engagement to George
- **Visits**: Visited with Rebecca when Miss Crawley called on Russell Square; came down with kind smiling looks; blushed kissing Rebecca; impressed Miss Crawley with "sweet blushing face"
- **Status**: Remains innocent of all developments; trusts George completely

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports; adored by men; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Engagement**: Engaged to Amelia; furious upon learning regiment knows; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her"
- **Recent**: Won two hundred pounds from Rawdon at billiards at Cocoa-Tree; had confided to Rawdon suspicions about Rebecca

**Other Characters**
- **Lady Crawley** [DECEASED]: Sir Pitt's wife; died during winter at Wilhaven; laid unwept and disregarded in vault full of strangers
- **Mrs. Firkin**: Witnessed proposal with Miss Briggs; wrote to Mrs. Bute Crawley reporting events; oversees young women servants at Park Lane
- **Miss Horrocks**: Butler's daughter at Queen's Crawley; took some of Rebecca's relics that Sir Pitt flung from her boxes
- **Old Mr. Osborne**: Wealthy merchant
- **Old John Sedley**: Family affairs troubled
- **Captain Dobbin**: Carried off George Osborne from billiards
- **Colan Lindson, Movie Lindson, Halan Hollwood, Nynelle Stenworth, Rozek Hollwood**: Secondary characters with minor narrative presence (various domestic scenes, conversations about weather, harvest, letters, river conditions; Colan's wife died of coughing sickness summer, buried at Bryngate)

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)
- **MARRIAGE REVELATION OCCURRED**: Rebecca's secret marriage to Rawdon discovered through letter left on pincushion, found by Miss Briggs early morning; intelligence reported to Mrs. Bute Crawley upon her arrival by Portsmouth mail
- **MISS CRAWLEY'S CRISIS**: Fainted and suffered hysterics upon learning Rebecca married to Rawdon; confined to bed; doctor and apothecary summoned; placed under nursing care of Mrs. Bute Crawley
- **SIR PITT'S FURY**: Upon learning marriage, broke into fury of language; became wild with hatred and insane with baffled desire; subsequently ransacked Rebecca's room at Queen's Crawley, destroying her belongings
- **REBECCA AND RAWDON'S POSITION**: Now living openly together in Brompton lodgings; awaiting Miss Crawley's recovery; Rawdon anxiously considers possibility she may not recover (potential loss of fifty thousand pounds inheritance)
- **MRS. BUTE'S INTERFERENCE**: Arrived at Park Lane morning of revelation; positioned herself as nurse to Miss Crawley and declared intention to assist; characterized Rebecca as "artful little hussy" and Rawdon as profligate; asserted crisis will reveal Rawdon's true character to Miss Crawley
- **NARRATIVE NOTE**: Narrator observes that if Rawdon had been present instead of nervously drinking claret at club, couple might have gone on knees before Miss Crawley, avowed all, and been forgiven; but this chance was "denied to the young couple, doubtless in order that this story might be written, in which numbers of their wonderful adventures are narrated--adventures which could never have occurred to them if they had been housed and sheltered under the comfortable uninteresting forgiveness of Miss Crawley"
